title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a typed page numbered '55 bis', printed upside down relative to the archive scan. It was evidently reused as scrap paper: the manuscript F-crystal computations of the previous page are presumably on its other side. Its content is a draft of the theory of semi-stable reduction of abelian varieties and Néron models. The numbering (3.4.0 reduction to strictly local S; 3.5 'critère galoisien de réduction semi-stable'; 4.1 filtration with three graded quotients (4.1.1); 4.3 independence of ℓ) matches SGA 7 I, Exp. IX, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'. So this is very probably a pre-publication version of SGA 7 IX §5, the part relating Barsotti–Tate groups and p-adic criteria.

Setting: S is the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and residue characteristic p. A_K is an abelian variety. T_ℓ(A_K) are Tate modules for all primes ℓ, including ℓ = p, where T_p means the Barsotti–Tate group A_K[p^∞] over η.

Proof of a theorem (5.13 presumably):
(a) is Prop. 5.10.
(b) The last assertion: for ℓ ≠ p, take K' corresponding to an open subgroup π' of Gal(K̄/K) whose intersection with inertia I lies in the kernel of the inertia action on T_ℓ. That kernel is open by hypothesis (5.12.1). This gives potential good reduction after a finite separable extension.
(c) Equivalence of three conditions, 1) ⇔ 2) ⇒ 3), with 3) ⇒ 1) remaining.
- For ℓ ≠ p this is the Galois criterion for semi-stable reduction (inertia acts unipotently).
- For ℓ = p, choose an auxiliary prime ℓ' ≠ p and reduce to S strictly local. Take a finite Galois K'/K with group G such that A_{K'} has semi-stable reduction.
- One must show that G acts trivially on the three graded pieces of the filtration T^t ⊂ T^f ⊂ T (toric part, abelian part, character part). Equivalently, the direct-sum representation is trivial, or its character is constant.
- By 4.3 this character is independent of ℓ' ≠ p. A later section 6.4 computes it in terms of T_p(A_K) as well. When T_p has 'bonne réduction virtuelle' (in the semi-stable sense), the computation gives a constant function, and the result follows.
- The marginal '(no-ℓ-)' flags this ℓ-independence/p-adic comparison argument.

Remark 5.13.1 is a conjecture. If a Barsotti–Tate group X_η over η has virtual good reduction over S, and 'essential virtual good reduction of level (échelon) n', then plausibly it has virtual good reduction of level n. The struck phrase notes this is what would have been used for the ℓ ≠ p case.
errors: No real error. The step 'trace constant ⇒ representation trivial' is valid for a finite group in characteristic 0, since characters determine representations and a constant character equals the dimension. It relies on the traces being integers independent of ℓ (4.3), as stated.
The ℓ = p case depends on a forward reference (6.4) not visible here, so completeness cannot be checked from this page.

ideas.what: Galois criterion for semi-stable reduction (inertia acts unipotently on T_ℓ)
Potential good reduction after a finite extension cutting out the inertia image (open kernel)
Proving the p-adic (T_p, Barsotti–Tate) semistable criterion by ℓ-independence of the character of G on the graded pieces (toric/abelian/character), computed also via T_p
ideas.modern_name: p-adic criterion for semistable reduction via p-divisible groups; independence of ℓ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck SGA 7 IX; later p-adic Hodge theory versions (Fontaine, Coleman–Iovita, Breuil)

ideas.what: Conjecture: for Barsotti–Tate groups, virtual good reduction + essential virtual good reduction of level n ⇒ virtual good reduction of level n
ideas.modern_name: extension of truncated BT groups / level of good reduction
ideas.where_published: possibly a remark in SGA 7 IX; unsure

missed.claim: Remark 5.13.1 conjectures that, for a Barsotti–Tate group with virtual good reduction, 'essential' virtual good reduction at level n implies virtual good reduction at level n. This is a statement about the level of truncation at which good reduction is detected. If it did not survive into SGA 7, it is a minor open thread, related to later results on truncated BT groups determining the BT group (Traverso, Vasiu, Lau).
missed.quote: Il semble plausible que si X_η est un groupe de Barsotti-Tate sur η qui a bonne réduction virtuelle sur S, et bonne réduction virtuelle essentielle d'échelon n, alors il a bonne réduction virtuelle d'échelon n.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It relates to effective bounds on the truncation level needed to detect or extend BT groups over DVRs. The topic is studied today, but the precise notion 'essentielle' is not standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft page of what became SGA 7 IX (semi-stable reduction, ℓ-independence, the p-adic criterion), material that is published and credited to Grothendieck. The only possibly unrecorded detail is the small conjectural Remark 5.13.1 on levels of virtual good reduction for BT groups.
transcription_corrections: Page is typed and printed upside down. It is a reused typescript sheet '55 bis' of an SGA 7 IX–type draft, not manuscript notes on crystals.
'en [-...-] {+termes+} de' : typed word struck and 'termes' written above; 'dans 6.4' has the 4 handwritten over another digit.
Marginal '(no-ℓ-)' is circled in pencil after 'démonstration.'; 'groupe' is inserted by hand in Remarque 5.13.1.
Handwritten line at the end reads roughly '(C'est ce qui aurait été utilisé pour voir) pour ℓ ≠ p.', with the first part struck out.
